advances: Actual caps with bounds tight at their own common budget; partial menus need not cover the mixed set or contain globally deepest marks. No obstruction is claimed for a rule retaining only globally justified cap constraints.

proof:
For each selected vertex $v_i$ choose a nonzero continuous functional on its full-dimensional fiber. Its closed upper-tail volume is continuous because all cutting planes are $d$-null, ranges from the full volume to zero at the support extremes, and is strictly decreasing between them since every intermediate strip contains interior points. Thus the required fraction $q/\pi_{v_i}\in(0,1)$ is attained by some proper cut. Choose a base exposing functional for $v_i$; the exposing margin is zero there and has a strictly negative finite gap at each other sampled base. Add a sufficiently large multiple to the own cut. Boundedness of the finitely many other fibers makes all their margins strictly negative, so the ambient capture fractions and mass are as claimed.

Let $m=\sum_zp_zz$ for an arbitrary positive posterior. A facet functional equal to $b$ on the facet and at most $b$ on $P$ is strictly smaller at $m$, since a full-rank $P$ has a base strictly off the facet. For a relation $\sum_i a_i(v_i-m)=0$ the facet functional then gives $\sum_i a_i=0$. Affine independence gives $a_i=0$ for all $i$. The covariance vectors are $(q/\pi_{v_i})p_{v_i}(v_i-m)$ with positive coefficients; adaptive-gaussian-active-cap-freezing forces zero adaptive covariance.

In the triangle calibration the closed cap is empty at $z=1,2$ since $\lambda_j\le1$. At zero its fraction is $(2/3)^2$ by homothety. At the uniform prior, $m=1$ and $c_j=(4/9)(1/3)(-1)=-4/27$; generally $m>0$ and $c_j=-(4/9)p_0m\ne0$. The three own caps cover the zero fiber since some barycentric coordinate is at least $1/3$. This is an obstruction with unchanged conditional laws, distinct from the source f7afca279c65bd1a's continuous-needle question.

In the ternary calibration, $v_i\cdot(z-v_i)\le-1$ at any other ternary base, so each cap is isolated and has own fraction $\Gamma_d$. For the listed columns $v_i-m$, subtract the column $v_0-m$ from the others to get $-2e_i$ for $i<n$. The absolute determinant is $2^{n-1}(1-m_n)>0$, also for $n=1$, since the strictly positive posterior includes bases with $z_n<1$. Multiplication by the positive factors $\Gamma_dp_{v_i}$ preserves rank. The selected groups leave other fibers uncovered. At the prior, every ambient containing cap of $(0,g_T)$ may be translated parallel inward to pass through it. For a through-mark oblique normal with base component $a$, at least half the base weight lies on $\{z:a\cdot z\ge0\}$ by base reflection, and on each such fiber the cap includes the corresponding centroid cut. This cut has fraction at least $\Gamma_d$ by 6769574fc1bd9f8d at full volume. A pure-base through-cap already retains at least half the weight. Thus the original center attains the asserted lower bound despite absence of a heavy fiber.

The general rank construction works for arbitrarily small $q$ even when the prior is not heavy anywhere. It establishes no active constraint at a larger budget $\alpha$ and no global cover; rank of such arbitrary retained caps alone therefore supplies no extra geometry of deepest marks.
statement:
For a finite base $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ of full affine rank, $n\ge1$, positive compact convex $d$-fibers, $d\ge1$, and positive prior $\pi_z$, fix $\alpha>0$. Choose $n$ affinely independent vertices $v_i$ of any facet of $\operatorname{conv}P$ and $0<q<\min\{\alpha,\pi_{v_1},\ldots,\pi_{v_n}\}$. There are actual ambient closed caps $H_i$ of original mass $q$ with capture fractions $g_i(z)=(q/\pi_{v_i})\mathbf1_{\{z=v_i\}}$. Their base covariance vectors span $\mathbb R^n$ at every positive posterior. Preservation of these active $q$-bounds forces $A_t=0$ in any existing adaptive Gaussian process of the stated type.

On $[0,2]\times T$ for the ordinary triangle, the caps $\lambda_j(X)-z\ge1/3$ have probability $4/27<2/9$, cover only the index-zero fiber, and each has scalar base covariance $-4/27$ initially and nonzero covariance at every positive posterior. On $[-1,1]^n\times T$ for a $d$-simplex, all $3^n$ original base probabilities are $3^{-n}<2^{-n}$. At the $n$ corners $v_0=\mathbf1$ and $v_i=\mathbf1-2e_i$ for $1\le i<n$, use the $d+1$ caps $\lambda_j(X)+v_i\cdot(z-v_i)\ge1/(d+1)$. They cover their respective selected fibers and have common original budget $\Gamma_d/3^n<\Gamma_d/2^n$, with full covariance rank at every positive posterior. The original point $(0,g_T)$ has normalized depth at least $\Gamma_d/2$.
title: Arbitrarily small actual cap menus can freeze adaptive base covariance
